findings.title: TEC2-1221WI is a ±5 V module, but it feeds the ±12 V rails
findings.detail: U2 is a TEC 2-1221WI. The datasheet lists that order code as a +5 VDC / –5 VDC, 200 mA output. Its outputs drive the nets +12V (pin 6) and -12V (pin 8), which supply the OPA2810 op-amps (U10, U11, U12 and others). Those rails are designed for ±12 V. The ±12 V part in the same family is the TEC 2-1222WI (83 mA per output). Either the part number or the rail names are wrong.
findings.failure_mode: With this part fitted, the op-amp stages get only ±5 V instead of ±12 V. Output swing and headroom fall far short of the design, so the analog signals will clip.

findings.title: U1 pin EN is floating / undriven
findings.failure_mode: A floating EN/CHIP_PU leaves the module in an indeterminate reset state — unreliable or no boot.
findings.citation: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 datasheet + hardware design guidelines: EN (CHIP_PU) must be pulled up (typ. 10k) with a delay cap; it must not float or the module may not boot reliably.

findings.title: U1 pin IO0 has no net for a required 100n
findings.failure_mode: A 1uF (instead of 100nF) cap on IO0 defeats the auto-download/reset sequence — can't flash without manual BOOT.
findings.citation: ESP32 auto-program circuit: IO0 uses a 100nF cap. A 1uF cap here (as on EN) is too large and breaks the auto-download timing.

findings.title: Board has malformed outline (no edges found on Edge.Cuts layer)
U16 input capacitors C2/C32 have no value
findings.detail: The only capacitors on U16's VIN rail (+5V) are C2 and C32. Both are generic 'C_Small_US' symbols with no capacitance value. The datasheet's typical circuit asks for a 1µF ceramic CIN (X5R/X7R). The output side is fine because it has several 10µF and 100nF capacitors.
findings.failure_mode: If the input capacitance is missing, too small, or not near U16, the LDO can ring or drop out during load steps from the ESP32 and display, especially since +5V also comes from the LM7805 output.
findings.excerpt: It is recommended to use X7R or X5R dielectric capacitor if 1.0 µF ceramic capacitor is selected as input/output capacitors.

findings.title: DevKit fed through both the 5V and 3V3 pins at once, which the datasheet says are mutually exclusive
findings.detail: U1 pin 21 (5V) is on +5V, which the LM7805 (U3) drives. U1 pins 1 and 2 (3V3) go through the 0 Ω resistor R31 to +3.3V, which the AP2112K (U16) drives. That puts the DevKit's own on-board 3.3 V LDO output in parallel with U16's output. When USB is plugged in, the DevKit's USB 5 V can also feed back onto the +5V rail. The DevKit guide lists 5V and 3V3 as two of three mutually exclusive ways to power the board.
findings.failure_mode: Two LDOs with paralleled outputs fight over the rail and share load unpredictably, and one can reverse-bias the other. A USB connection can back-drive the 7805 output and the analog 5 V rail. Pick one supply path: either leave R31 unfitted and use the DevKit's 3V3 as an output, or stop feeding the 5V pin.

findings.title: VREF/RFB driven by op-amps on ±12V rails, equal to the ±12V absolute maximum
findings.detail: U8 VREF (pin 7) is driven directly by U4 OUT (gained_func), and RFB (pin 8) by U5 OUT; both OPA2810s are powered from +12V/-12V. The AD5452 absolute maximum for VREF and RFB is ±12V, so there is no margin: any rail tolerance above 12V, or a saturated or overdriven gain stage, can put these pins at or past the limit.
findings.failure_mode: If the gain stage saturates (from too much input gain or at power-up) while the rails are slightly high, VREF/RFB can go beyond ±12V and damage the DAC's R-2R ladder. Limit the signal swing to the ±10V operating range or add clamping.
findings.excerpt: VREF, RFB to GND −12 V to +12 V

findings.title: ILI9341 module datasheet unavailable; DS1 connections not verified
findings.detail: There is no datasheet for DS1 (ILI9341 TFT module), so its pinout could not be checked against a source. Two netlist facts need an engineer to review them. First, SDO(MISO) on pin 9 is not connected, so the MCU can never read from the display. Second, the touch controller's T_DOUT goes to its own GPIO6 instead of sharing a MISO line. Pin 8 (LED) is driven straight from GPIO17. Whether that is safe depends on whether the module has its own backlight transistor or resistor.
findings.failure_mode: If the module has no backlight driver, GPIO17 might be overloaded by the backlight current. The pin assignments also cannot be confirmed without the datasheet.

findings.title: TS5A23157 datasheet unavailable; SW3 not verified
findings.detail: No datasheet could be found for SW3 (TS5A23157 module), so its pinout, the logic of its control inputs, and its bypass requirements could not be checked against the manufacturer's spec. Its connections are: V+ to +3.3V, IN1/IN2 to GPIO21/GPIO47, COM1/COM2 to the AD9833 outputs, NO1/NO2 to R3/R16, and NC1/NC2 to func_in.
findings.failure_mode: If the module's pin mapping or supply needs differ from what the schematic assumes, the waveform path to the function generator channels could be wrong.

findings.title: U1 pin EN has no net for a required 10k
findings.failure_mode: Missing EN pull-up => no defined power-on reset delay.
findings.citation: ESP32-S3 hardware design guidelines: EN uses a ~10k pull-up to 3V3 plus a 1uF delay cap (RC reset).

findings.title: U1 pin IO0 has no net for a required 10k
findings.failure_mode: Missing IO0 pull-up can leave the module entering download mode unexpectedly.
findings.citation: ESP32-S3 hardware design guidelines: IO0 (boot strap) needs a pull-up (typ. 10k) so the module boots to flash by default.

findings.title: U1 pin 3V3 is on 'Net-(R31-Pad1)', expected a net containing '3.3'
findings.failure_mode: Module supply off the 3.3V rail is out of spec.
findings.citation: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 datasheet, Pin definitions (3V3): module supply is 3.3V.

dropped.title: TEC2-1221WI outputs ±5 V but drives the ±12 V rails
dropped.detail: U2 is a TEC 2-1221WI. The datasheet lists this model as a +5 V / –5 V, 200 mA dual-output converter. On this board its outputs feed the nets +12V (pin 6) and -12V (pin 8), which supply the OPA2810 op-amp V+/V- pins. The ±12 V version in the same series is the TEC 2-1222WI (83 mA per output). Either the part number or the rail design is wrong.
dropped.failure_mode: The analog rails come up at ±5 V instead of ±12 V. The op-amp output swing and headroom are far below what the design expects, so the signal chain clips or doesn't work as intended.

dropped.title: DevKit powered through both 5V and 3V3 pins at once (mutually exclusive)
dropped.detail: U1.21 (5V) is on +5V from the LM7805 (U3), and U1.1/U1.2 (3V3) go through a 0 Ω resistor (R31) to +3.3V, which the AP2112K (U16) also drives. The DevKit has its own 3.3 V LDO, so the board's U16 output and the DevKit's LDO output end up tied in parallel. The datasheet says the 5V and 3V3 pins are mutually exclusive ways to power the board. On top of that, plugging in the DevKit's USB connectors back-feeds VBUS onto the external +5V rail.
dropped.failure_mode: Two LDOs fight on the same 3.3 V rail, so the current sharing is uncontrolled and the rail can be pulled to the higher output. If USB is plugged in while the 7805 is powered, current can flow backward into the 7805 or the USB host. Fix: leave R31 unfitted and use the DevKit's 3V3 as an output, or stop feeding the 5V pin.

dropped.title: AP2112 input/output capacitors have no value
dropped.detail: The +5V input capacitors C2 and C32 and the 3.3V output capacitor C33 next to U16 are all labelled with the generic symbol name 'C_Small_US' and have no capacitance value. The datasheet needs at least 1µF ceramic (X5R/X7R) on both CIN and COUT. Other caps on +3.3V (C23–C26, 10µ) probably meet COUT if they are placed close to the regulator, but the BOM must still give values for C2, C32 and C33.
dropped.failure_mode: If unvalued parts get the wrong value (or are left off), the LDO may oscillate or regulate poorly when the ESP32 draws load steps.
dropped.excerpt: It is recommended to use X7R or X5R dielectric capacitor if 1.0 µF ceramic capacitor is selected as input/output capacitors.

dropped.title: ILI9341 module datasheet not available; DS1 connections unverified
dropped.detail: No datasheet could be found for DS1 (ILI9341 TFT module), so I could not check its pins against a datasheet. Two things need a manual check. First, the LED pin is driven straight from GPIO17 (U1.10), so confirm the module has its own backlight transistor or resistor and that the backlight current is within what the GPIO can supply. Second, SDO(MISO) is left unconnected while T_DOUT goes to GPIO6, which is fine if the firmware never reads back from the display.
dropped.failure_mode: If the module has no backlight driver, the backlight current may exceed what the ESP32 GPIO can supply. The pin connections cannot be confirmed without the datasheet.
